Pan Am pilot. Doctor. Lawyer. Two and a half million dollars in fake checks, across twenty-six countries, all before he turned twenty-one.
That's the legend of Frank Abagnale. A bestselling book. A Spielberg movie. Decades on stage, teaching the world about fraud.
But in 2020, a writer named Alan Logan tried to check the story. Not the movie. The paperwork.
New York State prison records list inmate two five three six seven: Frank Abagnale. Locked up from July 1965 to December 1968.
Ages seventeen to twenty. The exact years of his most famous cons.
And the federal check case that finally put him away? Ten forged checks. Less than fifteen hundred dollars.
Back in 2002, Abagnale admitted part of it: I impersonated a doctor for a few days. In the book, it's like I am doing this for a year. Today, he denies telling any lies.
So maybe the greatest con was never the checks. Maybe it was the story you already believed.
